title.narrative: PSE 3 – Integrated Responses to Threats to Maritime Safety and Security in the Gulf of Guinea Maritime Domain in West and Central Africa

description.narrative:
The present peace and stabilisation engagement document provides the objectives and management arrangements for the peace and stabilisation cooperation concerning Danish support to the objective of:
"Strengthened regional approaches to maritime security in the Gulf of Guinea through enhanced joined-up responses to shared threats, and support the implementation of the Yaoundé Code of Conduct, including addressing gender and maritime women, peace, and security. "
The Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Centre (KAIPTC) in Accra, Ghana, will focus on Gulf of Guinea maritime security institutions and countries, particularly those within Zones E, F and D, including Benin, Cameroun, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Nigeria.

title.narrative: A platform for regular consultative research seminars on maritime security established.

Five (5) dialogue events for 250 national and regional maritime security practitioners (M/F), of which (3) expert events devoted to experts in the context of the research knowledge developed by the project, and two (2) events devoted to issues around coordinated implementation of regional maritime norms in the Gulf of Guinea maritime domain.

actual.value:
(A) A research seminar was held on 27 and 28 June 2023 to review and validate the six (6) studies that were conducted by the KAIPTC in 2022 - two of which focused on at-risk women in the maritime sector. The seminar was attended by 34 maritime security and governance experts (from state and non-state institutions) across the Gulf of Guinea region.
(B) Policy dialogue on trends and impact of illegal, unregulated and unreported (IUU) fishing in the Gulf of Guinea region was held in Abidjan from 14-18 May 2023. The dialogue provided a platform for stakeholders to share experiences, best practices, and strategies for sustainable fishing in the GoG. A total of 38 participants (28 males, 10 females) participated in the dialogue. Participants were drawn from 7 countries which are Benin, Cote d'Ivoire, Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, and Togo.

(A) The project team carried out one (1) consultative visits to five (5) countries including Ghana, Nigeria, Cote d'Ivoire, Cameroun, and Congo Brazzaville. The objective of the visits was to introduce the project to some key stakeholders and seek their buy-in and critical inputs for implementation.
Institutions consulted during the visits included ECOWAS, ICC, CRESMAO, and CRESMAC, national navies, fisheries commission, local artisanal fishermen, media groups, women's groups, ports and harbours, maritime administrations, and petroleum agencies.

title.narrative: A Code of Maritime Practice for Women in the Gulf of Guinea Maritime Domain developed and endorsed by at least seven (7) governments of countries that are signatory to the Yaounde Code of Conduct.

target.value:
(A) Two (2) published research papers on at-risk women in the maritime or coastal domains.
(B) Activities for cooperation with UNODC on Maritime WPS training course agreed and incorporated in KAIPTC annual implementation plans for 2022/23.

actual.value:
(A) The target of publishing 2 papers on at-risk women in the GoG region has been achieved.
With the third phase of the project having women in the maritime security space as one of the major focal areas, part of the research activities focused on understanding the role and impact of insecurities on women in the GoG maritime domain. The topics explored include understanding the multiple roles of women in maritime security and the impact of maritime criminality on women's livelihoods. Issues of the impact of maritime criminalities on women and the role they sometimes play as enablers have been overlooked over the years. The research, therefore, aims to contribute to addressing this gap.
(B) Activities for collaboration between KAIPTC and UNODC for the WPS training manual and training were initiated during the year under review. As a result, the KAIPTC included plans for further collaborations with the UNODC in its 2023 Implementation Plan.

(A) The two research papers have been conducted and to be published in H2 of 2024. The first focuses on women in maritime security and the integration of women into maritime security structures, with Senegal as a case study. The second explores the experiences of women in the maritime security sector from the grassroots to the top levels.
(B) From 19-20 July, the KAIPTC held a symposium under the theme "Harnessing the role of women in the blue economy". The two-day event brought together 48 (36 females, 12 males) participants from over 10 GoG countries.
(C) A 3-day high-level consultative meeting was held in Yaounde from 5-7 September. The meeting provided a platform for discussions on gender disparities and measures to promote women's empowerment in the maritime sector. 35 participants (27 males, 8 females) including leaders from the maritime industry, CSOs, et. participated in the event.
(D) The WPS Code of Practice has been developed in English and French.
